findings: vcpkg release cadence and volume: <cite index="42-3,42-4,42-5">302 ports were updated in July... as part of the 2026.07.29 registry release and the 2026-07-13, 2026-07-24, and 2026-07-27 tool releases, these updates include major SBOM improvements in vcpkg-tool, 302 updated ports including multiple major library upgrades</cite>. Earlier months show similarly high churn: <cite index="47-3,47-6">521 ports were updated in May... This release includes major library updates for Boost 1.91, Qt 6.11, and OpenCASCADE 8.0, along with 27 new ports and over 500 port updates</cite>, and <cite index="49-3">415 ports were updated in February and 321 ports were updated in March</cite>.

Registry growth trend across 2026: total ports rose from <cite index="49-1">There are now 2,773 total ports available in the vcpkg curated registry</cite> (Feb-Mar 2026) to <cite index="42-1">There are now 2,858 total ports available in the vcpkg curated registry</cite> (Jul 2026), i.e. roughly 85 net new ports added in five months despite continual removals of stale ones, e.g. <cite index="42-16">7 ports were removed as part of ongoing registry maintenance</cite> in July alone.

Individual flagship-library maintenance: gRPC was actively bumped inside the registry: <cite index="42-14">Notable port updates include grpc 1.76.0#1 -> 1.81.1</cite>. Boost issues coordinated cross-library releases: <cite index="21-1">The Spring 2026 release of Boost comes with upgrades to 25+ libraries and the new Boost.Decimal, of particular interest to quants and numerical programmers</cite>, and community summaries continue quarterly: <cite index="29-3">During Q2 2026 Boost work is summarized: boost::container::hub accepted for Boost 1.92; Boost.Unordered added C++20 range support; Boost.MultiIndex got iterator pointers; Boost.ICL fixed for libc++ v22</cite>. Asio shows a dated recent stable release: <cite index="26-1">Stable release: 1.38.2 / July 19, 2026; 60 days ago</cite>. nlohmann/json's latest major release is dated and feature-bearing: <cite index="31-1">Release date: 2025-04-11</cite> for v3.12.0. Dlib also shows a recent dated release: <cite index="30-1">Stable release: 20.0.1 / 29 March 2026; 18 days ago</cite>.

Repository-level community health signal (disclosed as a raw popularity/activity proxy only, not a standalone score): <cite index="42-11">The main vcpkg repo has over 7,700 forks and 27,300 stars on GitHub</cite>, up from <cite index="43-11">over 7,400 forks and 27,000 stars</cite> a few months earlier, indicating sustained contributor growth.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.limitations_of_proxy: Port-update counts and GitHub stars/forks are disclosed as raw, consistently-collected proxies alongside dated release evidence; they are not used as the sole basis for the score.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.raw_measurement: vcpkg (the largest curated C++ registry) ships monthly registry releases with hundreds of port updates per month and steady growth in total ports; Boost ships a structured, twice-yearly formal release plus continuous community/mailing-list activity; flagship individual libraries (nlohmann/json, Asio, Dlib, gRPC) show recent, dated releases.
metric.package_ecosystem_activity_mainte.score_rationale: 85/100. The dominant curated registry (vcpkg) demonstrates near-continuous, high-volume maintenance (hundreds of port updates monthly, monthly release cadence, steady net growth), and flagship domain libraries (Boost, Asio, nlohmann/json, gRPC, Dlib) all show recent, dated, substantive releases within the last 6-18 months. Score is not higher because C++ package activity is split across multiple non-interoperable package managers (vcpkg, Conan, Spack, system managers) rather than one unified registry, which dilutes any single ecosystem-wide activity signal and increases the risk of stale or duplicate/abandoned recipes across registries relative to ecosystems with one authoritative, first-party package index.

findings: vcpkg registry breadth: <cite index="42-1,42-2">There are now 2,858 total ports available in the vcpkg curated registry, a port is a versioned recipe for building a package from source, such as a C or C++ library.</cite> Microsoft's own overview states <cite index="20-5">Over 2300 open-source libraries to choose from in a curated registry, routinely built to verify ABI compatibility.</cite>

Foundational/general-purpose domain: Boost is treated as a standards-adjacent reference; <cite index="25-2">Beginning with the ten Boost Libraries included in the Library Technical Report (TR1) and continuing with every release of the ISO standard for C++ since 2011, the C++ Standards Committee has continued to rely on Boost as a valuable source for additions to the Standard C++ Library.</cite> Boost itself spans linear algebra, threading, image processing, regex, and unit testing in one umbrella: <cite index="24-1">The Boost C++ Libraries (also known simply as Boost) are a set of libraries for the C++ programming language that provides support for tasks and structures such as linear algebra, pseudorandom number generation, multithreading, image processing, regular expressions, and unit testing.</cite>

JSON domain: nlohmann/json is a mature, feature-rich, actively developed header-only library with multi-format support (JSON, BSON, BJData): <cite index="31-6,31-7">The BJData mapping now supports draft 3, including optimized binary array types, and the BSON mapping has added support for unsigned 64-bit integers.</cite>

Async/networking domain: Asio is a dedicated, long-running cross-platform async I/O library: <cite index="26-1,26-2">Asio is a freely available, open-source, cross-platform C++ library for network programming, it provides developers with a asynchronous I/O model.</cite>

Numerical/ML domain: Dlib is a general-purpose, cross-platform C++ ML library with continued releases: <cite index="30-1">Dlib is a general purpose cross-platform software library written in the programming language C++</cite>

Database/GUI/compression/CLI/messaging domains are also directly covered inside vcpkg's popular-ports catalog, e.g. <cite index="17-1,17-2">MySQL Server, the world's most popular open source database, and MySQL Cluster... SQLite is a software library that implements a self-contained, serverless, zero-configuration, transactional SQL database engine</cite>, GUI via <cite index="19-7">Simple DirectMedia Layer is a cross-platform development library designed to provide low level access to audio, keyboard, mouse, joystick, and graphics hardware via OpenGL and Direct3D</cite>, and CLI flag parsing via <cite index="17-13,17-14">The gflags package contains a C++ library that implements commandline flags processing, it includes built-in support for standard types such as string and the ability to define flags in the source file in which they are used</cite>.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.limitations_of_proxy: Port/recipe counts and presence in vcpkg/ConanCenter are used only as declared, disclosed evidence of breadth, not as the sole scoring input; qualitative domain-by-domain library maturity and standards-adjacency were the primary basis for the score.
metric.third_party_library_availability_.raw_measurement: C++ has mature, independently-maintained libraries covering every one of the 8 predeclared domains, distributed through at least two large curated package registries (vcpkg with 2,858 ports as of July 2026; ConanCenter with roughly 1,200+ recipes historically and continued growth).
metric.third_party_library_availability_.score_rationale: 93/100. Every predeclared domain has at least one long-tenured, actively-maintained, widely-distributed library, and most domains have 2+ independent competing options. Score is not 100 because coverage is split across multiple non-unified package managers (vcpkg, ConanCenter, Spack, system package managers) rather than one canonical first-party index, which fragments discoverability relative to languages with a single official package registry.

predeclared_sampling.candidate_universe_note: Full candidate universe per domain = all vcpkg ports (2,858 as of the July 2026 registry release) and all ConanCenter recipes, filtered to the domain by category tag; the highest-tenure/most standards-adjacent candidate per domain was frozen as the target below.

domains_and_targets.rule: Official first-party Microsoft-maintained C/C++ package manager, used as the denominator for domain-coverage breadth
Explicitly relied on by the ISO C++ Standards Committee as a source for standard-library additions since 2011
Longest-tenured, most widely vcpkg/ConanCenter-listed header-only JSON library for modern C++
Reference async I/O implementation accepted into Boost after formal peer review and maintained standalone since 2003
Long-running (since 2002) general-purpose ML/numerical library with a Wikipedia-tracked stable-release cadence
Google-maintained reference RPC framework, tracked as a named curated vcpkg port with version-pinned updates
De facto standard testing frameworks referenced by most C++ build-system and CI documentation
fmt is the reference implementation that became the basis for C++20 std::format; spdlog is its most common logging counterpart

predeclared_sampling.retrieval_route: public web search of official project sites, GitHub releases pages, Microsoft C++ Team Blog 'What's New in vcpkg' posts, and Wikipedia infobox stable-release fields
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: For each of 8 predeclared functional domains needed by typical application/systems software, the target library was fixed BEFORE evidence collection using a language-neutral, externally observable criterion: (a) presence and curated status in Microsoft's official vcpkg registry (a first-party, non-benchmark-affiliated C/C++ package manager) AND/OR (b) explicit recommendation/inclusion as the de-facto reference implementation cited by the C++ Standards Committee or major C++ tooling docs. Where more than one library qualified, the one with the longest continuous curated-registry presence and most recent registry-tracked update was selected. This mirrors the same two-route (package-index curation + official/standards-adjacent recommendation) rule that will be applied identically to every other language in this evaluation.
